strings.d1.s0.name: Marienplatz
strings.d1.s0.tips: Glockenspiel at 11:00 (and 12:00, plus 17:00 in summer). The New Town Hall tower lift costs 6 EUR.
strings.d1.s1.name: Frauenkirche
strings.d1.s1.tips: Cathedral with twin onion-domed towers. Look for the Devil's footprint.
strings.d1.s2.name: Viktualienmarkt
strings.d1.s2.tips: A food market since 1807. Try Weisswurst (by tradition eaten before noon), Obazda (spiced cheese spread) and the beer garden.
strings.d1.s3.name: Asamkirche
strings.d1.s4.name: Hofbräuhaus München
strings.d1.s4.tips: A beer hall dating from 1589: Mass (litre) beers, Schweinshaxe (roast pork knuckle) and a brass band. You share long tables with locals.
strings.d1.b0.name: Augustiner Bräustuben
strings.d1.b0.tips: The brewery's own hall, a local alternative to the Hofbräuhaus.
strings.d1.b1.name: St. Peter's Church Tower (Alter Peter)
strings.d1.b1.tips: 306 steps up to views over Marienplatz. An alternative to the Frauenkirche.
strings.d2.s0.name: Munich Residence
strings.d2.s0.tips: The Wittelsbach palace, with the Antiquarium, the treasury and the Cuvilliés Theatre.
strings.d2.s1.name: Hofgarten
strings.d2.s1.tips: Palace garden with the Temple of Diana.
strings.d2.s2.name: Eisbachwelle
strings.d2.s2.tips: Surfers ride a river wave in the middle of the city, all year round.
strings.d2.s3.name: Chinesischer Turm Biergarten
strings.d2.s3.tips: Beer garden by the Chinese pagoda in the Englischer Garten. You can bring your own food; try Brezn (pretzel) and Steckerlfisch (fish grilled on a stick).
strings.d2.s4.name: Englischer Garten Monopteros
strings.d2.s4.tips: Larger than Central Park. The Greek-style temple on the hill gives city views, and you can take a rowing boat on Lake Kleinhesselohe.
strings.d2.b0.name: Seehaus im Englischen Garten
strings.d2.b1.name: Alte Pinakothek
strings.d2.b1.tips: Dürer, Rubens, Rembrandt. Entry is 1 EUR on Sundays. A good option instead of the park when it rains.
strings.d3.s0.name: Nymphenburg Palace
strings.d3.s0.tips: Baroque summer palace with the Gallery of Beauties and the Amalienburg. The park is free.
strings.d3.s1.name: Nymphenburg Palace Park
strings.d3.s2.name: Schlosscafé im Palmenhaus
strings.d3.s2.tips: Greenhouse café for lunch in the palace park.
strings.d3.s3.name: Olympiapark
strings.d3.s3.tips: The tent roofs of the 1972 Olympics. The Olympic Tower viewing platform costs 13 EUR.
strings.d3.s4.name: BMW Welt & Museum
strings.d3.s4.tips: BMW Welt is free and the museum costs 10 EUR. Next to Olympiapark.
strings.d3.b0.name: Olympiaturm Restaurant
strings.d3.b1.name: Pinakothek der Moderne
strings.d3.b1.tips: Modern art and design. An alternative to BMW.
strings.d4.s0.name: Dachau Concentration Camp Memorial Site
strings.d4.s0.tips: 45 minutes by S2 and bus. Memorial to the first concentration camp, free entry, audio guide 4 EUR. Heavy going, but important.
strings.d4.s1.name: Dachau Altstadt
strings.d4.s1.tips: Old town and palace garden for a quiet break.
strings.d4.s2.name: Schwabing Leopoldstrasse
strings.d4.s2.tips: Bohemian district with the Siegestor and cafés.
strings.d4.s3.name: Café Luitpold
strings.d4.s3.tips: A coffeehouse since 1888. Try the Prinzregententorte.
strings.d4.s4.name: Glockenbachviertel
strings.d4.s4.tips: Gay-friendly neighbourhood with bars and Gärtnerplatz.
strings.d4.b0.name: Bratwurstherzl Viktualienmarkt
strings.d4.b0.tips: Nuremberg sausages next to the market.
strings.d4.b1.name: Lenbachhaus
strings.d4.b1.tips: Home of the Blaue Reiter (Kandinsky, Marc). An alternative to Schwabing.
strings.d5.s0.name: Neuschwanstein Castle
strings.d5.s0.tips: 2.5 hours by train and bus (Bayern-Ticket) or on a tour. Ludwig's fairy-tale castle. Book your timed ticket online weeks ahead; the climb takes 30 minutes.
strings.d5.s1.name: Marienbrücke
strings.d5.s1.tips: The bridge with the postcard view of the castle. It may be closed in winter because of ice.
strings.d5.s2.name: Hohenschwangau Castle
strings.d5.s2.tips: Ludwig's childhood castle. Combined ticket available.
strings.d5.s3.name: Alpsee Lake Walk
strings.d5.s3.tips: Mountain lake below the castles, with swans.
strings.d5.s4.name: Füssen Altstadt
strings.d5.s4.tips: Medieval town. Try Käsespätzle (cheese noodles) before the train back.
strings.d5.b0.name: Schlossrestaurant Neuschwanstein
strings.d5.b1.name: Tegelbergbahn
strings.d5.b1.tips: Cable car to an Alpine summit. An alternative to the lake.
strings.d6.s0.name: Deutsches Museum
strings.d6.s0.tips: The world's largest science and technology museum, with a mine, aircraft and a planetarium.
strings.d6.s1.name: Isar River Walk
strings.d6.s1.tips: River island and banks. In summer people swim and barbecue here.
strings.d6.s2.name: Wirtshaus in der Au
strings.d6.s2.tips: Bavarian inn specialising in Knödel (dumplings), in the Au district.
strings.d6.s3.name: Müllersches Volksbad
strings.d6.s3.tips: Art nouveau swimming pool from 1901, with a sauna.
strings.d6.s4.name: Gärtnerplatz
strings.d6.s4.tips: Round square with a theatre. Best in the evening.
strings.d6.b0.name: Der Pschorr Viktualienmarkt
strings.d6.b1.name: Deutsches Museum Verkehrszentrum
strings.d6.b1.tips: Transport museum. An alternative to the baths.
strings.d7.s0.name: Theresienwiese & Bavaria Statue
strings.d7.s0.tips: The Oktoberfest grounds (September to October). Take in the view from the head of the Bavaria statue.
strings.d7.s1.name: Augustiner-Keller Biergarten
strings.d7.s1.tips: Beer garden for 5,000 under chestnut trees. Have a Mass and a Brezn for your farewell.
strings.d7.s2.name: Munich Central Station
strings.d7.s2.tips: The S-Bahn to the airport takes 40 minutes. Farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Dallmayr
strings.d7.b0.tips: Luxury delicatessen and café at Marienplatz. Good for souvenirs.
strings.d7.b1.name: Alter Botanischer Garten
strings.d7.b1.tips: Park beside the station. An alternative to Theresienwiese.
strings.note0: A day ticket on the MVV costs about 9 EUR; the S-Bahn to the airport takes 40 minutes. For Neuschwanstein, take the Bayern-Ticket (train and bus) or a tour.
strings.note1: Summer temperatures are 25-30°C. Enjoy the beer gardens and the Isar, and surf at the Eisbach. Oktoberfest runs for the last 2 weeks of September (hotel prices triple).
strings.note2: A Mass of beer costs 15 EUR (16+ at Oktoberfest), a Brezn 2 EUR, Schweinshaxe 20 EUR. You can bring your own food to a beer garden. When tipping, round up the bill.
strings.note3: Weisswurst is eaten before noon and the skin is peeled off. Serve it with sweet mustard.
strings.note4: Museums cost 1 EUR on Sundays (the Pinakothek galleries). Book Neuschwanstein tickets online weeks ahead.
strings.note5: The Dachau memorial is free and open on Mondays. Be quiet and respectful.
